items.markdown:
If you’re looking around **Middlesbrough**, I’d be cautious about choosing purely on “blue” colour. Blue is a recognised Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour under the current Kennel Club standard, but health and responsible breeding should come first. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/o4fhe5lf/nov-25-kcj-final-online-1.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### Places to start looking

- BowesK9s in Guisborough is a nearby dog breeder worth contacting to ask specifically whether they currently have, or plan, Staffordshire Bull Terrier litters. **I haven’t verified that they currently have blue Staffy puppies available**, so ask before travelling.
- [S.A.R.A. The Ann Prosser Foundation](https://www.s-a-r-a.org.uk/) in Redcar and [RSPCA Great Ayton Animal Centre](https://www.rspca.org.uk/local/aboutus/contactus/-/rspca/great-ayton-animal-centre) are also local options if you’re open to adopting a Staffy rather than buying a puppy.
- I’d also use the **Kennel Club's breeder resources** and Staffordshire Bull Terrier breed-club networks rather than relying on adverts that prominently advertise “rare” or “exclusive” colours.

### Questions I'd ask any breeder

Before paying a deposit, ask:

1. **“Can I see the puppy with its mum, where the puppies are being raised?”**
 You should see the mother interacting normally with the litter. Be wary of anyone wanting to meet you in a car park or deliver the puppy without letting you see its home.
2. **“What health testing have both parents had, and can I see the certificates?”**
 For Staffies, the Kennel Club's current health guidance includes DNA testing for **hereditary cataracts (HC-HSF4-2)** and **L-2-HGA**, plus eye testing; elbow testing is also recommended as part of best practice. The breed also has a breed-club health scheme including patella testing. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/cvef530x/kc_health_standard_07-25-web.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/qvffqvwg/kc_health_standard.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **“What are the parents' registered names and Kennel Club registration numbers?”**
 This lets you independently check their pedigree and recorded health information rather than taking screenshots or verbal claims at face value.
4. **“Why did you choose these two dogs to breed?”**
 A responsible breeder should be able to explain temperament, health, conformation and genetic considerations—not just colour.
5. **“Have either parent had any health problems?”**
 Ask specifically about skin problems, allergies, eyes, joints, breathing, seizures and temperament, and whether there are relevant problems in previous generations.
6. **“What socialisation have the puppies had?”**
 Ask what they've experienced: household noises, handling, children, other dogs, grooming, car journeys, etc.
7. **“What happens if I can't keep the dog?”**
 A good breeder should want the dog returned to them or otherwise help rehome it rather than simply saying it's your problem.
8. **“Will the puppy be microchipped, vaccinated and vet-checked before collection, and what paperwork comes with it?”**

### One important point about “blue”

Don't let a breeder use **“blue,” “rare blue,” “blue-grey,” or “exclusive colour”** to justify a premium or distract from health testing. Blue itself is an accepted Staffy colour under the Kennel Club standard. [The Kennel Club](https://www.thekennelclub.org.uk/media/o4fhe5lf/nov-25-kcj-final-online-1.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
